newsitem.title: USA: Middlesex County creditors delay action after bill.
newsitem.headline: Middlesex County creditors delay action after bill.

text.p: Creditors of Middlesex County, Mass., agreed to delay their bid to attach the county's property, after some 25 Massachusetts state legislators introduced a bill that would eliminate Middlesex County government, a spokeswoman for the bill's author, Rep. Jim Marzilli, said.
The county's creditors include Fleet Financial Group Inc, Mellon Bank Corp unit Dreyfus Corp, the Middlesex Retirement Board and Marriott International Inc unit Marriott Management Services Corp.

The Middlesex County Retirement system has an unfunded pension liability in excess of $235 million, of the which the county's share is $38.7 million, according to a 1995 Coopers & Lybrand estimate. The remaining obligation is shared by 64 municipalities that belong to the system.

Under Marzilli's legislation, the cities and towns that make annual $2.86 million in payments to the county would instead make payments to the state, which would assume the county's liabilities. Marzilli estimated that those assessments would continue for about 25 years until the debt was retired.
Middlesex Superior Court Judge Hiller Zobel set a March 12 hearing to review the measure's progress.
The county defaulted on $4.5 million of revenue anticipation notes in December.
The measure, "An Act to Abolish Middlesex County Government" -- authored by Marzilli, D-Arlington, and co-signed by some 25 other lawmakers -- was introduced on Beacon Hill Friday.

The state's largest county and home to both Harvard University and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology has incurred about $17 million of debt largely through the inefficient operation of the Middlesex County Hospital, Marzilli noted.
